from pychrono import ChLinkManager, ChSystem, ChSystemNSC
from pychrono import ch_physical as phys
from pychrono import ch_ros as ros

import numpy as np


# Initialize PyChrono environment

ch = ChSystemNSC()


# Add physical systems and objects

# HMMWV vehicle with specified parameters

vehicle = phys.ChSelectFrictionSurfNSC(name='vehicle')

vehicle.set_friction_model(phys.ChCoulombFrictionSurfNSC(mu=0.8))

vehicle.set_restitution_model(phys.ChRestitutionSurfNSC(e=0.2))


# Terrain with defined friction and restitution

terrain = phys.ChSelectTerrainNSC(name='terrain')

terrain.set_friction_model(phys.ChCoulombFrictionSurfNSC(mu=0.6))

terrain.set_restitution_model(phys.ChRestitutionSurfNSC(e=0.3))


# Add vehicle and terrain to the link manager

link_manager = ChLinkManager()

vehicle.attach_to(link_manager)

terrain.attach_to(link_manager)


# Set necessary default parameters

# Engine type, tire model, and other parameters

vehicle.set_engine_type(phys.ChEngineNSC(name='engine', power=1000))

vehicle.set_tire_model(phys.ChTireNSC(name='tire'))


# Initialize driver system for vehicle control

driver = phys.ChDriverNSC(name='driver', max_force=500)

vehicle.attach_driver(driver)


# Integrate ROS for communication

ros_manager = ros.ChRosManager(ch)

ros_manager.register_ros_handler(ros.ChClockSynchronizer(ros_manager))

ros_manager.register_ros_handler(ros.ChDriverInputHandler(ros_manager, vehicle))

ros_manager.register_ros_handler(ros.ChVehicleStateHandler(ros_manager, vehicle))


# Simulation loop

sim_time = 10.0  # Simulation time in seconds

time_step = 0.01  # Time step in seconds

for t in np.arange(0, sim_time, time_step):

    # Synchronize and advance the vehicle, terrain, and driver systems

    ros_manager.sync_ros_handlers()

    vehicle.step(time_step)

    terrain.step(time_step)


    # Update ROS manager for data publishing

    ros_manager.update_ros_handlers()


# End of simulation

print("Simulation completed.")
